data.gender_notes: Leocadia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Leocadia is derived from the Latin word leo, meaning 'lion', and cadia, meaning 'strength' or 'power'. This name was given to several saints in early Christian history, including a 4th-century martyr and a 9th-century Spanish abbess. Leocadia is associated with the light of God's glory and the strength of faith. The name Leocadia carries the meaning “Light, Glory” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Latin. Parents who choose Leocadia usually hope their child will grow to embody light, glory and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: לאוקדיה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: לאוקדיה (Leocadia) היא שם נשים שמקורו ביוונית, שמשמעותו 'קבוצה של חזיונות של נשים' (Leokadia) , המורכב מ-לאוס (Leos), 'לבוש' ו-קאדיה (Kadia), 'קבוצה'. השם מופיע ב-Biblical Reference: לאוקדיה, סנטוריה (St. Leocadia of Toledo) ב-5 באפריל 60. השם הוא Saint Name. השם משמש גם ב-Hebrew Christian tradition, כשם לבן של-Christians.

in_greek.name: Λεωκάδια
in_greek.meaning: 集団の視覚的イメージ
in_greek.long_meaning: Λεωκάδια (Leocadia) είναι ένα γυναικείο όνομα που προέρχεται από τη λατινική, που σημαίνει '集団の視覚的イメージ' (Leokadia) , που αποτελείται από Λέος (Leos), '衣服' και Καντία (Kadia), '集団'. Το όνομα εμφανίζεται στη Βιβλική Αναφορά: Λεωκάδια, Αγία Λεωκάδια (St. Leocadia of Toledo) στις 5 Απριλίου 60. Το όνομα είναι Αγία Ονομασία. Το όνομα χρησιμοποιείται επίσης στο Ελληνική Χριστιανική παράδοση, ως όνομα για το γιο του Χριστιανών.

in_latin.name: Leocadia
in_latin.long_meaning: Leocadia est nomen femininum originis Graecae et Latinorum, quod significat 'collectio imaginum feminarum' (Leokadia) , compositum ex Leos, 'vestitus' et Kadia, 'collectio'. Nomen apparit in Biblicae Referentia: Leocadia, Sancta Leocadia (St. Leocadia of Toledo) in 5 April 60. Nomen est Nomen Sanctae. Nomen utitur in Christiana Traditione Latina, ut nomen filii Christianorum.

The name Leocadia is associated with the virtue of chastity and purity. It is also associated with the qualities of modesty and humility. In modern times, the name Leocadia has been used as a given name for girls, symbolizing the qualities of femininity and spiritual purity.

historical_references.reference: Leocadia of Seville was a virgin martyr and saint, venerated in Spain. She is believed to have lived in the late 3rd or 4th century. According to legend, Leocadia was the daughter of a wealthy Roman nobleman named Seneca. When her father died, she refused to marry any man and instead dedicated her life to God. She was discovered by the Romans and persecuted for her faith. She was executed by having her body pierced with lances, and her remains were taken to Seville and buried in a crypt. The shrine of Leocadia became an important pilgrimage site in medieval Spain.

Leocadia of Tomis was a Christian martyr and saint, venerated in Romania. She is believed to have lived in the 5th century. According to legend, Leocadia was a noblewoman in the city of Tomis (now Constanta, Romania). She was a convert to Christianity and was persecuted during the reign of Emperor Valentinian III. She was tortured and beheaded for her faith, and her remains were taken to a church dedicated to Saint Peter. The cult of Leocadia spread throughout the Balkans and was particularly strong in Dalmatia.
